Dhenā denotes a ‘milch cow,’ or in the plural, ‘draughts of milk.’ In two passages Roth takes the word to mean ‘mare,’ and in another the ‘team’ of Vāyu's chariot. Benfey, on the other hand, renders it ‘lips’ in one passage, with Sāyaṇa and with Durga's commentary on the nirukta. Geldner assigns to the word the senses of ‘lips,’ ‘speech,’ ‘cow,’ ‘beloved,’ and ‘streams.’

Dhenu in the Rigveda and later means ‘milch cow,’ which is often mentioned with special reference to the production of milk, and is contrasted with the ‘bull’ (vṛṣabha, pumāṃs, anaḍvāh). In the plural the word denotes ‘draughts of milk.’ The derivative, dhenukā, means merely ‘female.’
